L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: Liechtenstein applies Swiss VAT law in a customs union with Switzerland. The general rate is 8.1% from 1 January 2024 (7.7% before). Businesses with domestic taxable turnover below CHF 100,000 in a financial year can be exempt from VAT liability. Rate confirmed by Kintsugi (2026).

sources.title: Liechtenstein - Corporate - Other taxes
sources.quote: The general VAT rate is 8.1% as of 1 January 2024 (7.7% up to 31 December 2023).

sources.title: Liechtenstein - Corporate - Other taxes
sources.quote: Any person liable for VAT that is involved in domestic entrepreneurial activity with a taxable turnover that is less than CHF 100,000 within a financial year can be exempted from taxation.

sources.title: Liechtenstein VAT Guide for 2026 (Kintsugi)
sources.quote: Liechtenstein applies the Swiss VAT system, with an 8.1% standard rate.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: none of the major platform barriers apply. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Send, receive, and withdraw in local currency'). (5) Stripe accepts merchants here, so you can take card payments directly on your own site. (6) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
